PHOTOSYNTHESIS vs CHEMOSYNTHESIS — PARALLEL PRIMARY PRODUCTION
================================================================

PHOTOSYNTHESIS                    CHEMOSYNTHESIS
  6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light              CO₂ + H₂S + O₂
       → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂                 → CH₂O + H₂SO₄
                                        (sulfur oxidation)
  Energy source: SUNLIGHT           Energy source: CHEMICAL
  Location: photic zone (0-200 m)   Location: any where geology
  Producers: phytoplankton,           delivers reduced compounds
    plants, cyanobacteria             (deep-sea vents, cold seeps,
  Global rate: ~120 Pg C/yr          shallow springs, caves)
  Requires: light                   Requires: reduced compound
                                      (H₂S, CH₄, NH₃, H₂, Fe²⁺)
                                      AND oxidant (O₂ or SO₄²⁻)

CHEMOSYNTHETIC REACTIONS (examples):
  Sulfur oxidation:   H₂S + CO₂ + O₂ → [CH₂O] + H₂SO₄
  Methane oxidation:  CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O  (aerobic)
  Anaerobic methane:  CH₄ + SO₄²⁻ → HCO₃⁻ + HS⁻ + H₂O
  Iron oxidation:     4Fe²⁺ + O₂ + 8H⁺ → 4Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O
  Nitrification:      NH₃ + O₂ → NO₂⁻ + NO₃⁻ (Thaumarchaeota)

HYDROTHERMAL VENT DISCOVERY TIMELINE
======================================

1960s:      Theory predicts thermal venting at mid-ocean ridges
            (plate tectonics + seafloor spreading = heat flux)
            But: no technology to test, no samples

1976:       Warm-water anomalies detected by temperature sensors
            at Galapagos Rift (Eastern Pacific spreading center)

February    DSV Alvin dive to Galapagos Rift at 2,500 m depth
1977:       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │  Geologists Jack Corliss, John Edmond, and      │
            │  colleagues expected: warm water, some bacteria  │
            │                                                  │
            │  Found:                                          │
            │  Dense fields of tube worms 2+ m long           │
            │  Mats of white bacteria                          │
            │  Giant clams, mussels, crabs                     │
            │  Shrimp swarming the vents                       │
            │                                                  │
            │  "Isn't the deep ocean supposed to be           │
            │   essentially empty?" — Jack Corliss              │
            └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1979-:      Follow-up dives establish chemosynthetic basis
            First proposal that bacteria in tube worm tissue
            → confirmed: endosymbiotic chemoautotrophs

Impact:     Rewrote the axiom that all life depends on sunlight
            Opened astrobiology to subsurface ocean worlds
            Won Nobel Prize territory (Corliss et al. recognized
            with multiple major awards but no Nobel given)

MID-OCEAN RIDGE HYDROTHERMAL SYSTEM
======================================

  SEAFLOOR                              SEAFLOOR
      │                                     │
      ▼  Seawater infiltrates cracks         ▼
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                     SEDIMENT                          │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                   BASALT CRUST                        │
  │   Seawater percolates down crack network              │
  │   Heated by magma chamber below                       │
  │   Chemical reactions with basalt:                     │
  │     SO₄²⁻ removed, Mg²⁺ removed                       │
  │     H₂S, CH₄, CO₂, metals (Fe, Mn, Cu, Zn) added      │
  └──────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │ Hot acidic fluid rises
                     ▼

BLACK SMOKER                         WHITE SMOKER
Temp: 350-400°C                      Temp: 40-300°C
(not boiling — pressure)             (cooler, mixing zone)
Color: black (metal sulfides:        Color: white (barium,
  FeS, ZnS, CuFeS₂ precipitate       calcium, silica minerals)
  on contact with cold seawater)     Chemistry: more oxidized
Chimney growth: cm/day                pore water mixing
Extreme conditions:                  Hosts: different
  obligate thermophiles,               microbial communities
  hyperthermophiles
  (Methanopyrus: 122°C)

FOCUSED vs DIFFUSE FLOW:
  Focused: black/white smokers — high T, chemistry intense
  Diffuse: cracks and mats — lower T (5-30°C above ambient)
    → Hosts more diverse, accessible biology
    → Where Riftia tube worms live
    → Where most vent invertebrates concentrate

blocks.heading_context: ## Riftia pachyptila: The Iconic Vent Animal
blocks.text:
RIFTIA PACHYPTILA — ANATOMY AND SYMBIOSIS
==========================================

  PLUME (red, feathery)  ← hemoglobin-rich; bright red
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Absorbs: O₂ and H₂S simultaneously from water   │
  │  Transport: simultaneous in blood (no mixture)   │
  │  Hemoglobin binds H₂S at separate site from O₂   │
  │  (unique adaptation — H₂S is lethal to other     │
  │   hemoglobin-carrying animals including humans)  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  WHITE TUBE (up to 2.4 m long)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Chitin/protein tube — structural support        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  VESTIMENTUM (trunk)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Anchors to tube; receives blood supply          │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  TROPHOSOME
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Specialized organ: up to 50% of body mass       │
  │  Packed with ENDOSYMBIOTIC BACTERIA              │
  │  ~10⁹ bacteria per gram of trophosome tissue     │
  │  Bacteria: Candidatus Endoriftia persephone      │
  │            (Gammaproteobacteria)                 │
  │  Reaction: H₂S + CO₂ + O₂ → organic C            │
  │            (thioautotrophy)                      │
  │  Host receives: organic carbon compounds         │
  │  Bacteria receive: H₂S, O₂, CO₂ delivered        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

FASTEST GROWTH RATE OF ANY MARINE INVERTEBRATE:
  Up to 85 cm/year under good vent conditions
  Rationale: vent activity is episodic; must grow fast
  to exploit productive phase before vent shifts/dies

COLD SEEP SYSTEM
================

CONTINENTAL MARGIN CROSS-SECTION
  ↑ Sea surface
  ↓
  WATER COLUMN
  ↓
  SEAFLOOR SEDIMENT (hundreds of meters thick on continental margins)
        │
        │  CH₄ generated by:
        │  1. Microbial methanogenesis (buried organic matter)
        │  2. Thermogenic breakdown of organic matter below
        │  3. Methane hydrate dissociation
        │
        ▼ Fluid seeps upward
  SEEP COMMUNITY:
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Surface mats: sulfide-oxidizing bacteria             │
  │    (Beggiatoa, Thioploca) — white bacterial mats      │
  │    visible from ROV — first sign of seep activity     │
  │                                                       │
  │  Carbonate rocks: precipitated from DIC produced      │
  │    during methane oxidation — hard substrate for      │
  │    chemosymbiotic bivalves (Bathymodiolus mussels,    │
  │    Calyptogena clams, vesicomyid clams)               │
  │                                                       │
  │  In sediment: ANME archaea consortia                  │
  │    (Anaerobic Methane Oxidizers)                      │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ANME ARCHAEA — REVERSE METHANOGENESIS
=======================================

Normal methanogenesis (methanogens):
  CO₂ + 4H₂ → CH₄ + 2H₂O   (or acetate → CH₄ + CO₂)

ANME reverse it:
  CH₄ + SO₄²⁻ → HCO₃⁻ + HS⁻ + H₂O   (AOM: anaerobic oxidation of methane)

  Energy yield: ΔG° = -17 to -40 kJ/mol (barely positive under these conditions)
  Living on this tiny energy margin requires: close syntrophic partnership

ANME-SRB (sulfate-reducing bacteria) CONSORTIUM:
  ANME archaea and SRB (Desulfosarcina, Desulfococcus) form
  tightly coupled consortia (physical aggregates, ~10-100 μm)
  ANME oxidize CH₄ → electrons/reducing equivalents transferred to SRB
  SRB reduce SO₄²⁻ using those electrons → releases HS⁻

  Net reaction eliminates both CH₄ and SO₄²⁻
  Global significance: ANME consume ~90% of methane rising from
  seafloor before it reaches the water column
  Without ANME: far more CH₄ would reach the atmosphere
  (CH₄ is 80× more potent GHG than CO₂ over 20 years)

OCEAN WORLDS WITH SUBSURFACE LIQUID WATER
==========================================

BODY              EVIDENCE FOR LIQUID WATER       HABITAT ANALOG
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Europa            Magnetic field perturbations     Deep-sea cold seeps
(Jupiter moon)    surface geology (chaos terrain)  Hydrothermal vents?
                  Plume activity (probable)         ANME-type reactions
                  Ice shell: 10-30 km thick         (no solar energy needed)
                  Ocean depth: possibly 100+ km

Enceladus         Active plumes confirmed           Cold seeps
(Saturn moon)     (Cassini flew through them)       Alkaline hydrothermal
                  H₂, CO₂, CH₄ detected in plume   (like Lost City:
                  Organic molecules detected         serpentinization-based,
                  Silica nanoparticles = hot water   not volcanic)
                  Ocean under ~20 km ice

Ganymede          Magnetic field = subsurface       Deep cold ocean
(Jupiter moon)    saline ocean                      Low likelihood of
                  Most massive moon in solar system  energy sources

Titan             Surface lakes of liquid methane   Unlikely — no water
(Saturn moon)     Not liquid water                  Different chemistry

WHY CHEMOSYNTHESIS MATTERS FOR ASTROBIOLOGY:
  Enceladus plumes contain all ingredients for sulfur-based
  chemosynthesis: H₂S, H₂, CO₂, liquid water, temperature
  gradient (warm vent → cold ocean)

  The Lost City hydrothermal field (Mid-Atlantic):
  Serpentinization-driven (not volcanic):
  Water + peridotite → H₂ + heat + carbonate
  → Alkaline vent (pH 9-11, T 40-90°C)
  → Unique community distinct from volcanic vents
  → Serpentinization can occur on any rocky body with water
  → Possible on Enceladus, Ganymede, Europa
